note: The scene-date Democrat, read through. T-0257 left c001-c003 as the fixture its schema was written against; T-0295 read the rest. The reading is made from the RECONCILED deposit transcription (`artifact_role: primary`), not from the `-2` rebuild this branch can open: the letter list is legible at name level in the primary and is not in the alternate. The segmenter cut each printed column in half and alternates the halves line by line, so almost every claim here is `interleaved` and most bracketed supplies are read off the OTHER half of the same printed lines — each claim's note says which lines those are. Nothing is supplied that the transcription does not carry somewhere.

claims.notes: INTERLEAVE. Lines 5040-5068 of the transcription alternate this advertisement with an unrelated bank notice; the quote is the fifteen lines that belong to Cohen and `lines_of_claim` names them. Line 5052 ('1018.') sits in the range and belongs to neither reading, so it is left out rather than assigned. OCR JUDGEMENTS, all rn/m-class or long-s confusions: 'WOrD'→'[WOULD]', 'tomere'→'[cus]tomers', 'india'→'India', 'kinka'→'kin[d]s', 'amme'→'[ex]amine', 'Mesers.'→'Messrs.', 'Nor. 3, 1634'→'Nov. 3, 1834'. THE DATELINE. '1634' cannot stand: the Democrat's run begins in November 1833 and this is Vol. II No. 11 of 1835-07-01, so the ad is a standing one placed 1834-11-03 and '-49' is its insertion count. WHAT IS NOT SUPPLIED. Line 5063 begins mid-word at the column edge: the transcription reads 'low Mesers. Newberry and Dole's' and the words before 'low' are cut away. T-0257's own text quotes them as 'a few doors below', and that phrase is not in this issue, so it is NOT supplied here — '[…]' marks the gap. A fuller witness may exist: Chicago Democrat 1834-06-04 line 2362 reads 'A,fec doors below Messrs. Nacberry & Dol'.' in a column that also names Peter Cohen, and settling whether that is this same standing advertisement is work for the Democrat read, not for this fixture.

claims.notes: INTERLEAVE, same column and the same alternation as c001. THE NAME. Line 5070 is cut after 'HOGA'; the final letter is restored on a second witness in this issue rather than guessed — the post-office notice at line 3705 of page 3 column 5 is signed 'HOGAN, P. M.'. Whether the postmaster and this merchant are one man is an identification this fixture does NOT make: no merge is declared in identity.json and the two would need one. THE PLACEMENT IS THE POINT AND IT IS INCOMPLETE. Lines 5075-5076 read 'in South Water Street, one' / 'the Post Office,' — whatever stood between them is cut by the column edge. T-0257's text quotes it as 'one [door from] the Post Office'; no witness in this issue supports 'door from', so the words are left unsupplied and '[…]' marks the gap. The anchor is documented either way. NO DATELINE. The ad carries the insertion code '2m5' (line 5080) and no 'Chicago, <date>' line, so `ad_copy_date` is null rather than inferred from the code.

claims.notes: RULING 1 — a listed name alone mints a resident candidate, and this claim is the fixture's worked example of one: `letter_list_only` is true here and the compiler carries it onto the person. THE LIST is the post office's, interleaved with advertising through page 3 column 5 and closed at line 3705 by its own notice, signed 'HOGAN, P. M.'. Every name in it is cut at the left column edge, which is why this one was chosen: the alternate transcription of the same issue (data/research/newspapers/text/chicago_democrat_1835_07_01__alt_transcription_2.txt, line 274) reads 'Work, James Houston' in full, so the initial W is restored on a SECOND WITNESS and not on the shape of the word. Neighbouring names have no such agreement — line 3652 reads 'hitney, Joshus' here and 'Whurney, Julian' there — and are left for the Democrat read to settle.

A name whose initial is present but disagrees with its section is a MISREADING, not a clipping, and stands as printed — correcting it would be a guess, and `identity.json` is the only place two spellings may become one person.
